text:
incident-bot: [PAGER] kv-cache eviction rate spike detected in eu-west-1 - sustained >15% rps for 12m, error budget risk. auto-escalation to #incidents triggered.
oncall: acked, jumping on. who owns KV allocator today?
helen: I can take triage for first 15m. looks like cont-batching windows also increased. seeing correlated latency cliffs on p99.
samir: adding context - we merged batch-window regression yesterday (r=PR#5321) which touched the continuous batching heuristics. suspect interplay with slab fragmentation.
aj: are we seeing cuda OOMs or pure eviction churn? metrics show free_slots dropping, eviction_count up, and active_arena_frag rising.
maria: any customer impact so far? CS reporting timeouts for some streaming customers in eu-west-1. ticket #CS-842 incoming.
cs-ledger-bot: CS-842 created: customer "WaveAnalytics" experiencing partial requests timed out, approx 4% of their calls in last 10m.
helen: ok plan: 1) revert continuous-batching change or throttle batch size; 2) temporarily increase kv-eviction-threshold; 3) enable arena-compaction job. low-risk order: throttle batching first.
oncall: agree, throttle batching to previous config. aj, can you push a hotfix for batch window and bump eviction threshold?
aj: will do. applying hotfix now — patching config in prod configmap. command: ```kubectl -n inference set env deploy/kv-proxy BATCH_MAX_WINDOW_MS=20 BATCH_MIN_WINDOW_MS=2 && kubectl rollout restart deploy/kv-proxy -n inference```
samir: also pushing runtime guard to fallback to small-batch variant if allocator fragmentation > 0.6. issuing canary to 10% nodes. command: ```rdctl runtime apply --policy small-batch-canary --selector region=eu-west-1 --percent=10```
helen: enabling arena compaction cron: ```kubectl -n infra apply -f arena-compact-cron.yaml``` (runs every 5m for next 30m).
helen: metrics after 2 mins: eviction rate down ~40%, p99 latency improving but still elevated. active_arena_frag stalled, compaction starting to free pages.
maria: CS updated WaveAnalytics: we pushed a mitigation and are monitoring, they saw drop in errors on a few calls. keeping them posted. :handshake:
oncall: good. monitoring for 20m, if steady we'll ramp canary to 50% then full. logging any regressions.
aj: canary logs show fewer cuda-malloc spikes, but one node reported repeated small OOMs; fallback engaged, requests routed to other nodes. no customer-impacting errors from fallback.
samir: investigating allocator metrics on the problematic node: arena slab churn correlates with a specific model serving variant (gpt-small-quant). suspect quantized KV page alignment causing wasted slabs. adding per-model slab limits as temporary measure.
helen: rolling per-model slab limits to eu-west-1, command: ```kvctl set-slab-limit --model=gpt-small-quant --limit=128MB --region=eu-west-1``` live.
maria: WaveAnalytics reports reconnection succeeded, error rate down to baseline. kudos. :tada:
cs-ledger-bot: CS-842 updated: customer acknowledged improvement, monitoring.
oncall: timeline note: root cause likely coupling of cont-batch heuristics + recent batching change + model-specific slab behavior triggering allocator fragmentation. follow-ups: deeper alloc profiling, add regression test for quantized model slab interactions, and a safer default batch cap.
aj: opened follow-up ticket ENG-1159 for allocator profiling + a unit test harness.
samir: also creating runtime fallback feature request to auto-detect slab fragmentation per model and apply conservative batch window. ENG-1160.
helen: postmortem owner? volunteering to drive doc and rollback criteria.
oncall: thanks helen. I'll schedule 1hr incident blameless postmortem, invite eng-runtime, eng-ml, oncall rotation, and CS. closing pager after 40m of stable metrics. :white_check_mark:
helen: final notes in case log dump helpful: saved heap profiles to s3://redwood-ops/incident-3981234567/ and exported allocator metrics dashboard link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/kv-alloc/alloc?orgId=1&from=now-1h&to=now
samir: leaving the small-batch canary at 50% for 2h then evaluate.
maria: notified account tier leads and flagged as high-touch until next release.
oncall: de-escating. great coordination everyone.
